name: Neck bridges / wrestler bridges
lead: A neck bridge, or wrestler's bridge, is a bodyweight position in which a person arches the back with weight supported on the feet and the head or neck, used in wrestling and combat sports and discussed in looksmaxxing circles as a way to thicken the neck. A general reference on the bridge exercise describes it as used in sporting and self-defense settings such as wrestling, judo and mixed martial arts, and as intended mainly for lower back and gluteal strength [1].

No studies of neck bridges for cosmetic neck thickness were found. Searches of the medical literature return mostly unrelated material, such as 'neck-bridge' devices used in aneurysm surgery, which are unconnected to the exercise.

paras: Bridge exercises generally involve arching the body so that only some points touch the ground; variations include single-leg and one-arm forms, which load the hamstrings, glutes and spinal erectors [1]. Wrestling and other grappling sports use bridging to escape pins, which is why the neck-supported version is associated with those sports [1].
The general bridge article does not discuss risks of neck-loaded bridging [1]. No clinical data on injury rates for cosmetic neck bridging were found.
No studies found. Medical literature on 'neck-bridge' devices concerns aneurysm treatment and is unrelated to the exercise.

card.summary: A wrestling-style arch on the head and feet used to thicken the neck; no appearance research exists.
card.note: No data on injury risk for this use; the source material is thin.

quick.overview:
A neck bridge is an arch where the head or neck helps support the body, drawn from wrestling and grappling sports.

It is mentioned as a way to thicken the neck. No studies have tested it for that purpose.
quick.mechanism: The position loads the neck and back muscles with bodyweight. General bridge references focus on back and glute strength.
quick.risks: No injury data for cosmetic neck bridging were found. Any risks are not documented in the available sources.
